set.overview: A long, steep day on the dry eastern flank of the Sierra crest, reaching the 13,494-foot summit of Mount Pinchot from the Owens Valley side. The route follows a loose talus chute out of Armstrong Canyon to the crest, crosses a high plateau, then follows the broad east ridge at class 2. The rock is crumbly igneous stone, so footing is the main challenge rather than technical difficulty.
set.approach: Drive the rough, narrow mining road up Armstrong Canyon west of Independence as far as your vehicle allows; the first switchback is loose volcanic cinder and rocks of varied size, so check current road condition first. From the end of the road, a faint climbers' path leads to the foot of a wide talus chute that rises nearly 2,000 feet to the crest.
set.descent_text: Return the way you came: down the east ridge, back across the rising talus to the head of the chute, then down the chute to the canyon floor. Fast travel down the loose talus is possible by sliding on the rock, but it sends debris downhill, so keep a large party spread out or on the chute's edges. Follow the climbers' path back to the road end.
hazards: Loose talus and small friable rock in the Armstrong chute make footing poor and send stones onto anyone below
Little or no water in the canyon above the road, so carry what you need
The access road is narrow with loose cinder at the first switchback and may stop a low-clearance vehicle short of the trailhead
Strong, shadeless sun on the Owens Valley side during a long summer day

review.notes: Gain and distance skipped: only one unopened snippet (SummitPost blocked with 403) gave 9 mi RT / 5000 ft; no figure read on an opened page for this line alone. Season skipped: only summer dates seen.

set.overview: Striped Mountain is a 13,179-foot Sierra Peaks Section summit on the crest south of Taboose Pass, named for its bands of dark and pale rock. The walk-up goes over Taboose Pass, then climbs the northeast slope on class 2 talus and sand to the top, with no technical climbing. The challenge is the long, steep Taboose Pass trail that must be climbed first.
set.approach: Start at the Taboose Pass trailhead at about 5,700 feet in the Owens Valley desert and hike the dusty, steep trail roughly eight miles and almost 6,000 feet to the pass. Cross a stream a few miles up, then drop slightly into the lake basin on the west side, where the peaks stand to the south of the trail and the northeast slope leads to the summit.
set.descent_text: Descend the same slope you climbed, or drop the east side toward the saddle between Striped and Goodale mountains if you plan to continue to Goodale. Otherwise return to the basin, then climb back over Taboose Pass and hike down the long trail to the trailhead.
hazards: A second climb over Taboose Pass on the return, after a long, steep and sun-exposed trail with little shade
Loose talus and sand on the upper slopes slow both the ascent and descent
A stream crossing a few miles from the trailhead can be wet in early season

review.notes: Source report rates the northeast slope class 2 while the row says Class 1; grade left alone. Gain and distance skipped: only combined two-peak day totals read; SummitPost 8.9 mi / 7800 ft seen only in a search snippet. Season skipped.

set.approach: Hike the Taboose Pass trail from the trailhead at about 5,700 feet, roughly eight miles and almost 6,000 feet of climbing to the pass. Continue into the lake basin northwest of the peaks, then work up to the saddle between Goodale and Striped mountains, where the west slope of Goodale begins.
set.descent_text: Reverse the route: down the west slope to the saddle, then straight down toward the main lake in the basin. From there go back up over Taboose Pass and descend the trail to the trailhead.
hazards: Steep, tedious talus on the way down from the saddle to the lake basin
The summit block is class 3, so a short hand-and-foot move is needed to stand on top
The Taboose Pass trail is steep, dusty and without shade, and must be climbed again on the way out
A stream crossing a few miles from the trailhead can run high in early season

review.notes: Gain, distance and season skipped: only combined multi-peak totals read.

set.overview: Cardinal Mountain is a 13,396-foot Sierra Peaks Section summit about a mile north of Taboose Pass. The approach is the long, steep Taboose Pass trail from the Owens Valley, and the climb itself is a class 2 ridge walk on loose scree and talus. It is a hard day because of the approach, but the summit is straightforward once the pass is reached.
set.approach: Start at the Taboose Pass trailhead at about 5,700 feet and follow the trail about eight miles to the pass, climbing almost 6,000 feet on a dusty, sandy track with very little shade. From the pass, leave the trail and head north toward Cardinal, taking care to aim for the correct peak, since parties have set off toward a neighbouring summit by mistake.
set.descent_text: Return the way you climbed, going down the loose scree on the ridge and slopes to the base of the peak, then back to the pass. Hike back down the Taboose Pass trail to the trailhead.
hazards: Loose scree on the descent makes for fast but unstable travel
Peak identification and route-finding from the pass can lose time
Hot, shadeless trail on the east side of the Sierra, with water scarce below the pass

review.notes: Gain and distance skipped: the one opened page gives only the trail to the pass (about 8 mi, almost 6,000 ft), not the summit. Season skipped.

set.overview: Kennedy Mountain is an 11,433-foot summit in Kings Canyon National Park, climbed by a long trail approach from Lewis Creek followed by a short, easy walk. The way goes through a burned forest to Frypan Meadow, then crosses country to Kennedy Pass, and finishes on sand and rubble slopes to the summit. The distance and the sustained climbing, rather than any hard moves, make it a full day.
set.approach: Start at the Lewis Creek trailhead and follow the Lewis Creek Trail through terrain burned in the 2015 Rough Fire, with little shade, crossing Comb Creek and Lewis Creek along the way. After about six miles the trail reaches Frypan Meadow, where it fades in wet ground; continue northeast cross-country, traverse the southern slopes of the mountain, then follow a trail that switchbacks up to Kennedy Pass about half a mile below the summit.
set.descent_text: Go back down the sandy slopes south of the summit to the creek, then retrace the route through the meadow and burned forest to the Lewis Creek trailhead. The route-finding through brush above Frypan Meadow is easier on the way back because the path is already pushed through.
hazards: Many downed trees and trail that disappears in meadows and overgrown drainages after the fire
Two creek crossings, Comb Creek and Lewis Creek, can be fast and deep during snowmelt
Dense manzanita, aspen and brush above Frypan Meadow slow cross-country travel
Loose sand and rotten rock on the summit ridge, with snow patches lingering early in the season
Hot, shadeless burned slopes on the lower trail

evidence.fact: 7400 ft gain, Lewis Creek trailhead round trip
20.7 miles round trip, halved to 10.35 miles one way = 16.66 km

review.notes: Gain and distance are from one trip report only (round trip halved); SummitPost's 10.3 mi / 7,700 ft was seen only in a snippet and the page returns 403. Season Jun-Sep is an inference from the reported early-season snow and creek runoff, not a stated window: reviewer may drop it.

set.approach: Start at the Copper Creek trailhead at Road's End and follow the Copper Creek Trail up the canyon to a cairn near the saddle below Mount Hutchings, just before Granite Basin. A use trail then leads cross-country to Grouse Lake, where you stay on the east side of the lake because cliff bands block the west shore.
hazards: Cliff bands along the west shore of Grouse Lake force the route to the east side
Loose sand and talus on the upper slopes make for slow, unstable footing
Lingering snow can cover the easier ground early in the season, leaving class 3 moves
Mosquitoes around Grouse Lake in early summer
